narrative.northStar: The Live Wire on the Drafting Table
narrative.overview:
Chat is presented as a working machine laid out on an engineer's sheet: a calm black ground, white type, and a dashed 1px grid that frames the page column and cuts it into bands. Nothing glows or floats. The only colour is a single emerald that marks things that are actually running: the light travelling down the stripe field, a check beside a real capability, a status pill in a preview. Everything else is monochrome zinc, so the eye goes to the product and to whatever is live.

Density is calm and generous. Sections breathe with roughly 100px of vertical air, headings are short and set in Urbanist at weight 500 with tight negative tracking, and supporting copy is small, light Geist in a muted zinc. The product itself is shown rather than described: rebuilt chat, source chips, a drafted bug ticket and an audit table, drawn in the same tokens as the page.

Dark is the default and the first thing a visitor sees; a near-white paper version mirrors every role. The page rejects the generic light SaaS template: a screenshot hero, pill eyebrows over every heading, rows of identical rounded cards, gradient washes.

This world currently governs the marketing page only (the `.landing` scope). See the scope note under Do's and Don'ts.
keyCharacteristics: Black ground (dark default) or warm paper ground (light), white or ink type, zinc secondary.
One emerald accent, reserved for live things.
Dashed 1px rails on both sides of the content column, dashed dividers between bands, small triangle markers where rails cross a divider.
Urbanist 500 display with -0.02em to -0.03em tracking; Geist for everything else.
Square-ish 4px controls, softer 10px/14px containers, flat surfaces with no shadows.
Buttons whose label slides up and is replaced by a copy of itself on hover.
Anything illustrative (testimonials, pricing, preview data) is labelled "Example".

rules.name: The Live-Only Rule
rules.body: Emerald appears only on something that is running, true or confirmed: the stripe field, checks, status, focus. It is never a button fill, a heading colour, a link colour or decoration. If you can't say what is live about it, it stays zinc.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: There is no secondary or tertiary accent. A second hue would compete with the single signal the page relies on.

rules.name: The Medium Display Rule
rules.body: Display and headline type is Urbanist at 500 with -0.02em to -0.03em tracking. No bold display, no all-caps headings, no positive tracking.

rules.name: The Bare Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings stand alone. No eyebrow, kicker, pill or small label sits above a heading.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift. Separate them with a line or a one-step tonal change, not a shadow or blur.

dos: Do use the line colour at 1px for every rail and divider, dashed for structure and solid for containers.
Do keep emerald for live things only: stripes, checks, status, focus, selection.
Do set display and section headings in Urbanist 500 with -0.02em to -0.03em tracking.
Do use 4px corners on buttons and chips, 10px on inner panels, 14px on outer cards.
Do label every illustrative testimonial, plan and preview as "Example".
Do show the real product, rebuilt in the page's own tokens, instead of a static screenshot.
Do honour reduced motion: pause marquees, freeze the stripe field, skip label slides and the theme reveal.
donts: Don't place an eyebrow, kicker, pill or small label above a heading.
Don't introduce a second accent colour, gradient wash or coloured button fill.
Don't use shadows or blur to separate surfaces.
Don't state invented results, customers or metrics, or present planned features as available.

Don't use the older shadcn zinc and blue tokens from `:root` and `.dark` inside the landing scope. Those still govern the sign in, sign up, chat and admin pages, whose move to this system is planned but not done; they are a known gap, not part of this system.
